items.topic: Where does initiative metadata live on the decision?
items.context: Today, accepting an initiative-proposal decision requires the operator to re-author the initiative payload by hand, which loses fidelity. The fix is to capture structured metadata (name, priority, depends_on, target_scenario, optional title) at decision-add time so accept can derive the create payload directly. The question is whether this metadata is a first-class structured field on the decision record or inferred at accept time from option labels / topic / notes.

options.label: Structured `initiative_metadata` field on the decision record
options.rationale: First-class field added to the decision proto + storage, populated via decision-add/decision-update, immutable after first accept (mirrors F15 modifications). Maximum fidelity; explicit; queryable; mirrors the just-shipped pattern. Recommended because it solves the exact pain point (hand-transcription) instead of papering over it.

options.label: Inferred from selected option + decision topic at accept time
options.rationale: No new field; auto-create derives initiative name from the selected option's label, title from the decision's topic. Lower implementation cost but doesn't address the description's core complaint that accept-time inference loses fidelity vs. what the team explicitly agreed to (priority, depends_on cannot be inferred).

options.label: Convention encoded in `notes` prose (e.g. YAML front-matter)
options.rationale: Reuse the existing notes field with a parsing convention. Cheapest but produces an unstructured contract; previous walks have already shown that prose-in-notes is the anti-pattern this entire initiative exists to retire.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.context: Once the metadata is captured, decide how the accept path actually fires the downstream initiative-create. Options range from automatic (zero ceremony, matches the operator's stated goal of 'one CLI call') to opt-in (safer but reintroduces friction).

options.label: Always-on when context=initiative-proposal AND metadata is present
options.rationale: Zero extra ceremony at accept time — exactly matches the description's goal ('the most common decision outcome'). Predictable: if the metadata block is on the decision, accept creates. Failure handled by d4. Recommended because the data model itself (presence of metadata) is the operator's signal of intent — captured deliberately at decision-add.

options.label: Opt-in `--auto-create-initiative` flag on decision-accept
options.rationale: Operator must pass the flag (or click a checkbox) at accept time. Safer if there's any ambiguity about intent, but reintroduces the second-action friction the item is trying to remove.

options.label: Interactive prompt asking 'create initiative now? [Y/n]'
options.rationale: Human-friendly but unworkable in non-interactive contexts (CI, scripted operator workflows, API). Would require both modes anyway.

options.label: Always-on, with `--no-auto-create-initiative` escape hatch
options.rationale: Hybrid: default to always-on (per A) but allow operators to skip in unusual cases. Adds surface area; consider only if d5 surfaces a strong reason to allow accept-without-create.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.notes: Make sure the cli output makes it clear that an initiative was auto-created, and gives command/location/etc. to find it. Also make sure it reminds you to add any more details/depends_on/etc. to the initiative as needed to ensure it’s well-constructed

items.topic: Cross-scenario seam between prompt-manager and swarm-manager
items.context: Decision records live in prompt-manager; initiatives live in swarm-manager. Auto-create requires the prompt-manager accept path to invoke swarm-manager's initiatives-create. There is no existing direct call between these scenarios. This is the boundary-of-responsibility decision and it shapes coupling, testability, and failure handling.

options.label: prompt-manager API calls swarm-manager initiatives API directly via internal Go client
options.rationale: Single API call from the operator's perspective. Coupling lives in one place (a typed client in prompt-manager that targets swarm-manager). Aligns with how scenarios already share Go modules. Recommended because failure paths and retries are easier to reason about in one process boundary; testable with a stubbed client.

options.label: CLI orchestrates two API calls back-to-back
options.rationale: prompt-manager API just persists the metadata; the CLI's decision-accept command calls prompt-manager-API then swarm-manager-API. Loose coupling, but breaks the API-equivalence promise (the API alone cannot fulfill the operator's intent), and the UI would have to replicate the orchestration.

options.label: Event/queue-based: prompt-manager emits an 'initiative-proposal-accepted' event consumed by swarm-manager
options.rationale: Truly decoupled; would scale to multiple downstream consumers. But the project has no existing event bus and adding one purely for this is over-engineering. Failure visibility is also worse.

items.freeform: Api to api via api-core/discovery package

items.topic: Failure semantics when initiative-create fails after decision-accept
items.context: If the operator's decision-accept succeeds in prompt-manager but the downstream swarm-manager initiative-create fails (duplicate name, validation error, transient outage), what state should the system end up in?

options.label: Decision still accepts; surface a structured warning with the create error; record `auto_create_status` on the decision
options.rationale: The team's deliberation outcome (accept) is independent of mechanical create-success. Avoids partial-rollback complexity. Operator sees the failure in CLI/UI and can retry via a new `decision-retry-auto-create` command (or just run swarm-manager initiatives create manually). Recommended because it preserves the integrity of the decision record, which is the source of truth.

options.label: Transactional all-or-nothing: if create fails, decision-accept also fails and reverts to its prior status
options.rationale: Cleaner mental model in the success case but very awkward to implement across two services without a distributed transaction. Operator would also lose their 'I agreed to this' record on transient failures.

options.label: Decision-accept blocks until create succeeds (retries internally)
options.rationale: Simple from the operator's view but couples accept latency to swarm-manager availability and gives no escape hatch for true failures (duplicate name etc).

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.topic: Behavior when context=initiative-proposal but `initiative_metadata` is missing on accept
items.context: If d1=A (structured field) and d2=A (always-on when metadata present), we still need to define what happens when a decision is tagged context=initiative-proposal but no metadata block was attached at decision-add time (e.g., legacy decisions, or operator forgot).

options.label: Accept fails with a clear error: 'add --initiative-metadata to the decision (or use decision-update) before accepting'
options.rationale: Forces the metadata to exist exactly when it can be authored from the decision's still-fresh context. Predictable, no silent fallbacks. Recommended because the whole point of this item is to eliminate hand-transcription — silent fallback would re-introduce it.

options.label: Accept succeeds; auto-create is skipped; operator drops back to the manual `swarm-manager initiatives create` flow
options.rationale: Maximum flexibility, no new failure modes, but reintroduces the exact pain the item is solving for any decision missing the block.

options.label: Auto-derive a minimal initiative from `decision.topic` + selected option + warn
options.rationale: Best-effort fallback. Better than nothing but produces low-fidelity initiatives (no priority, no depends_on) — which is the original complaint.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.text: Sibling F15 (`prompt-manager-decision-partial-accept-with-modifications`) just shipped the structured `modifications` field and an immutable-after-accept rule. This plan deliberately mirrors that pattern (immutability, `--initiative-metadata-file=<path>` escape hatch, contract doc in `scenarios/prompt-manager/docs/reference/`) and propagates `modifications` into the generated initiative's description so the accepted scope-shaping signals don't get lost in the cross-scenario hop. Contract path on disk: `scenarios/prompt-manager/docs/reference/decision-modifications-contract.md` (verified to exist).

Decision struct already has a `Context string` field (`scenarios/prompt-manager/cli/teams/teams.go:194,228`) — `initiative-proposal` flows through today as a free-form tag with no special handling. Added behavior keys off this exact value, so no schema migration of `Context` itself is needed.
